subject: koala
pitch: A sleepy koala hugging a eucalyptus branch. Soft ash-grey fur with a cream chest and cream-lined fluffy ears, a big black leathery nose, half-closed drowsy brown eyes, strong grey paws with dark claws, and a sprig of blue-green eucalyptus leaves in one hand, mid-munch.
reasoning:
I'm picturing a koala hugging a horizontal eucalyptus branch, sitting upright with one arm wrapped around it and the other hand bringing a leafy sprig to its mouth mid-chew.

A front-facing trunk would block the face, so I'll go with the sitting pose instead. I'm working out the branch and post dimensions for the display stand, then building the spine chain joints from hips through chest to neck with pear-shaped body radii and cream belly shading.

Now I'm detailing the head: a wide-scaled sphere for the skull, fluffy round ears with cream inner discs, and an elongated black nose positioned at the front of the snout.

Eyes get small brown spheres positioned half-closed, with a grey hemisphere dome placed over the top half to act as a drooping eyelid, slightly tilted forward for a sleepy koala look. I'm also planning a separate lower jaw joint attached to the head for mouth articulation.

Working out the jaw and arm placement: the lower jaw gets a small cream-grey sphere positioned to look slightly open mid-chew, maybe with a leaf tucked in the mouth corner. For the arms, I'm placing shoulders symmetrically and routing the left arm down and around the branch so the hand drapes naturally over the front, adjusting the hand position to overlap slightly with the branch for a convincing hug.

Now I'm setting up elbow bend angles and paw details with small claw cones, then positioning the right arm so the hand brings the leaf up to the mouth, calculating distances from shoulder to hand to keep it within reasonable limb lengths. For the legs, I'm placing the hips and bending the thighs forward-out so the feet can hook onto the front of the branch for a sitting pose.

Now I'm defining the leaf sprig geometry, with a stem running from the koala's hand up to near its mouth, decorated with lance-shaped eucalyptus leaves in blue-green tones plus some rounder juvenile leaves, positioning the stem path and leaf cluster near the mouth.

I'm adding a side twig with painted bark grain in brown-grey tones, then setting up fur coloring with an ash grey base, lighter highlights on the ear fluff, and a cream tone for the chest countershading.

Now I'm placing the head directly on the body with no visible neck, matching koala anatomy, and positioning the muzzle and nose spheres slightly forward and cream-grey in color while adding small cream tufts around the ear rims.

I'm working out exact eye placement so they sit precisely on the curved head surface rather than floating inside it, solving for the correct z-depth given the head's ellipsoid dimensions.

For the ears, I'm positioning them as flattened discs near the top sides of the head, scaled to look like rounded koala ear shapes angled slightly outward.

Working out the ear tuft positions using angle-based offsets rotated around the Y axis to match the ear's outward tilt, placing nine small cream spheres for fluff. Now I'm moving on to the torso and rump, thinking about adding a sitting bum pad shape for the koala's pose.

Figuring out where a cream belly patch goes along the spine tube — since the path runs mostly upward, I'm reasoning that the back side faces the "normal" direction and the front/belly sits around the 180-degree mark, so I'll place a cream sector there for the chest and belly. For the skeleton, I'm setting up the spine chain rooted at the hips joint, using a catmull-rom curve through a few points to build the sweep, with the head joint parented to the top of the spine.

Adding head and jaw joints...

I'll add a dark flattened sphere for the mouth interior, skip the tail entirely, and move to building a branch using a curved sweep anchored to the hip joint since that's the only available root.

I'm adjusting the branch to be its own joint parented to hips rather than riding directly on the koala, then placing support posts and flaring the feet down to meet the floor. I'll position the koala's hips a bit higher on the branch so the rump pad covers the overlap without hiding the legs.

Now I'm nudging the spine curve upward and adding more forward curvature toward the head, repositioning the eyes, nose, muzzle, and ears to match, and checking that the overall height still reads as a stylized (if slightly tall) sitting koala. I'm also setting shoulder and hip joint positions and working out leg bend angles so the feet reach their floor targets with natural-looking knee bends.

I'm now working out the arm placements: adjusting the left arm's length so the hand wraps around the branch with a paw and claws, and positioning the right arm so the hand can bring a eucalyptus sprig up to the mouth, solving for elbow bend angles that make each reach look natural.

Then I'm designing the sprig itself—plotting a stem path from the hand to the mouth, and fanning several leaves off the lower part of the stem at varied outward angles, figuring out the extrusion directions so each leaf gets proper thickness along its width and length.

I'm placing roughly seven small leaves alternating sides along the stem, then setting up a similar twig-with-leaves attachment at the branch end, reusing a helper function to add leaf clusters along any path.

Alternating leaf colors between a few muted greens, and attaching leaves to the correct rigid bone—using the tip joint of each limb chain for sprigs. For the chain setup itself, I'm parenting arm chains to the spine joint and leg chains to the hips, passing in point arrays as polylines.

Now I'm working out paw details: spheres scaled flatter at the hand joint, with small dark cones as claws, oriented downward for the left paw and upward/forward for the right. I'm also setting up mottled fur paint sweeps across the body, cream sectors on the chest, and darker tones on the paws, applying the same fur paint treatment to the limbs.
